_comment: Rivals (Expansion 6 F.2, docs/ADVENTURES.md 5.6; game/story/rivals.py): a band after the same prize as you. `chance` by blueprint that a tale has one; `clock`: the days before you meet them (`meet_after`), the days their race takes once met (`race_days`), how often something of theirs may happen (`every` days, `event_chance` a night), how much of the villain's hit points they take with them when they die in its hall (`wounds`), what they ask for the prize by tier (`price`, in copper). `kinds`: a hero of the land with companions, a band of deserters, a lord's child with paid swords: their weight, the relation they start at (-2 to 2), their leader and band by tier (the leader is the first that fits the party's budget, the band fills it), the most of them by tier, and their words. `fates`: the epilogue's line for each way it ended. Words: {rival} (first name), {rival_full}, {rival_band} (them as a band), {rival_who} (what they are), {prize}, {they}/{their}... for the leader.

who: a sword for hire with a name in every inn from here to the coast
a hunter of bounties who has outlived three companies
one of the heroes they sing about in {town}, older now than the songs
band_words: {rival} and the three who ride with {them}

who: a sergeant who walked away from a lost war and took {their} section with {them}
the last of a free company that broke its contract and ran
a deserter with a price on {their} head and a plan to pay it off
a lord's {child} with a borrowed sword and a purse of {their} father's silver
the youngest {child} of a great house, out to win the name the eldest was given
a lord's {child} who has paid good coin for swords and means to be seen using them

slain: {rival_full} died by your hand, over {prize}. In {town} they do not say which of you was in the right.
{rival_full} wanted what you wanted, and is dead for it. You buried {them} by the road, which is more than {they} would have done for you.
Nobody sings of {rival_full}. You saw to that, on a cold day, over {prize}.
lair: {rival_full} went into {home} ahead of you. You found what was left. When the tale is told in {town}, {their} name is the one that makes them quiet.
{rival_full} got there first. That is all anyone says of {them} now: that {they} got there first.
You found {rival_full} in {home}, and you did not tell {town} how. Some things should not be told twice.
overrun: {rival_full} sent for help when {they} needed it, and help did not come. {Their} band was found on the road a week later.
{rival_full} died out there, alone with {their} band, waiting for you. Nobody blames you. Not aloud.
{rival_full} is dead, overrun where {they} had made {their} stand. You were asked, and you did not go.
prize: {rival_full} rode off with {prize}, and sold it, or kept it, or lost it at dice; the tales disagree.
{rival_full} won that race. {They} still tell{s} the story of it in the inns, and {they} tell{s} it well.
{prize} hangs on {rival_full}'s wall now, and {they} will show it to anyone who asks.
bought: {rival_full} sold you {prize} and drank the price in {town}. {They} speak{s} well of you, which is something.
You paid {rival_full} for what you should have had for nothing. {They} took the silver with a grin, and {they} earned it.
friend: {rival_full} kept the truce, to the end and after it. When you pass through {town}, the first drink is {theirs}.
You and {rival_full} wanted the same thing, and in the end you shared it. {They} speak{s} of you as a friend.
{rival_full} rides on, somewhere, and when {they} hear{s} your name, {they} raise{s} a cup to it.
fought: {rival_full} came when it mattered, as {they} swore {they} would, and stood with you at the end.
At the end {rival_full} came over the hill with {their} band, and that was the turn of it. {They} tell{s} it differently, and better.
{rival_full} kept {their} word and came to the last fight. In {town} they drink to the both of you.
gone: {rival_full} gave it up in the end and rode away. You do not know where {they} went.
{rival_full} was beaten to it, by you, and took it badly, and left.
{rival_full} went home with nothing to show but the road. {They} will not forget your name.
fell_beside: {rival_full} sent for you when {they} needed you, and you came, and {they} died anyway, beside you, with {their} sword in {their} hand.
{rival_full} fell in the fight you rode to, with you beside {them}. In {town} they say {they} died glad of the company.
You came when {rival_full} called, and it was not enough. {They} died beside you, and you buried {them} where {they} fell.
late: {rival_full} came to {home} the day after it was over, and found you had been first.
{rival_full} rode in too late, saw what you had done, and rode out again without a word.
{rival_full} heard how it ended from a stranger in an inn, and paid for the stranger's drink, and left.
